from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Elastic collisions conserve momentum and kinetic energy.",
            "A small block hits a large block.",
            "The large block slides toward a wall.",
            "These laws govern simple mechanical motion.",
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Elastic Collisions", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects
        m_block = Square(color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.6).scale(0.3)
        M_block = Rectangle(color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.6).scale(0.6)
        m_label = Text("m", color="#E0FFFF").next_to(m_block, UP, buff=0.1)
        M_label = Text("M", color="#E0FFFF").next_to(M_block, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        blocks = VGroup(m_block, m_label, M_block, M_label)
        self.place_in_area(blocks, 'B2', 'C5', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.add(blocks)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        momentum_txt = Text("Momentum: m*v1 + M*v2 = Const", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        energy_txt = Text("Energy: 0.5*m*v1^2 + 0.5*M*v2^2 = Const", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        equations = VGroup(momentum_txt, energy_txt).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(equations, 'D2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(equations))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(m_block.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1.5))
        flash = Flash(m_block.get_right(), color=WHITE, line_length=0.2)
        self.play(flash)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(M_block.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1.0))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Collisional Setup", [
            "We track collisions between two blocks and a wall.",
            "Mass ratio changes the collision count.",
            "The hamster hits the sumo wrestler."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        wall = Line(UP, DOWN, color=GREY).scale(1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(wall, 'C1')
        wall_label = Text("Wall", color="#FFFFE0", font_size=20)
        wall_label.next_to(wall, LEFT)
        
        m_block = Square(color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.3)
        M_block = Square(color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.7)
        
        m_label = Text("m", color="#FFFFE0", font_size=20)
        M_label = Text("M", color="#FFFFE0", font_size=20)
        
        m_group = VGroup(m_block, m_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)
        M_group = VGroup(M_block, M_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(m_group, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(M_group, 'C5')
        
        collision_count = 0
        counter_text = Text(f"Collisions: {collision_count}", color="#90EE90", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(counter_text, 'B4')
        
        self.add(wall, wall_label, m_group, M_group, counter_text)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFE0")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#90EE90")
        # Animate bounce
        path = VGroup(m_group)
        for _ in range(3):
            self.play(path.animate.move_to(self.grid['C2']), run_time=0.5)
            self.play(path.animate.move_to(self.grid['C4']), run_time=0.5)
            collision_count += 1
            counter_text.become(Text(f"Collisions: {collision_count}", color="#90EE90", font_size=24).move_to(self.grid['B4']))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFB6C1")
        # Increase M size
        self.play(M_block.animate.scale(1.5), run_time=1)
        # Frequent bounces
        for _ in range(5):
            self.play(path.animate.move_to(self.grid['C3']), run_time=0.2)
            self.play(path.animate.move_to(self.grid['C4']), run_time=0.2)
            collision_count += 1
            counter_text.become(Text(f"Collisions: {collision_count}", color="#90EE90", font_size=24).move_to(self.grid['B4']))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Mathematical Mapping", [
            "Mass ratio 100^n gives n+1 digits of Pi.",
            "System phase space maps to circular motion.",
            "Collisions act as a digits calculator.",
            "Pi emerges from simple physical rules.",
            "Visual representation of the correlation."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display M = 100^n * m
        eq = MathTex("M = 100^n \\cdot m", color="#00BFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(eq, 'B2', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(eq))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00BFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display 31 and Pi
        num_31 = Text("31", color="#FFD700", font_size=48)
        pi_approx = MathTex("\\pi \\approx 3.14159...", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(num_31, 'C2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_approx, 'C4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(num_31), FadeIn(pi_approx))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Visualize a circle
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE)
        line = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color=RED)
        phase_space = VGroup(circle, line)
        self.place_in_area(phase_space, 'D3', 'F5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(circle), Create(line))
        self.play(Rotate(line, angle=2*PI, about_point=circle.get_center(), run_time=2))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Placeholder for asset
        asset_label = Text("[PiCollisionGraph]", font_size=20, color=GRAY)
        self.place_at_grid(asset_label, 'F1', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(asset_label))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GRAY)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Unfolding", [
            "Represent velocities as vectors in 2D.",
            "The wedge angle depends on mass ratio.",
            "Light beams hit edges π/θ times.",
            "The system measures Pi geometrically."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Represent velocities as vectors in 2D.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        wedge = VGroup(
            Line(ORIGIN, 3 * RIGHT + 1 * UP, color="#FFA500"),
            Line(ORIGIN, 3 * RIGHT + 1 * DOWN, color="#FFA500")
        )
        self.place_in_area(wedge, 'B3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(wedge))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The wedge angle depends on mass ratio.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Light beams hit edges π/θ times.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        dot = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'C3')
        self.add(dot)
        
        path = VMobject(color="#D3D3D3")
        path.set_points_as_corners([self.grid['C3'], self.grid['D4'], self.grid['B5']])
        self.play(Create(path), MoveAlongPath(dot, path))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # The system measures Pi geometrically.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF00FF")
        count_text = Text("Bounces: 3", color="#FF00FF", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(count_text, 'F5')
        self.play(Write(count_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Intuition", [
            "Nature hides constants in chaotic systems.",
            "Conservation laws reveal deep mathematical truths.",
            "Physics effectively calculates fundamental numbers."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        sum_text = Text("Conservation laws can calculate digits of π.", color=WHITE, font_size=24)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        block_small_group = VGroup(block_m_small, block_m_small_label)

        self.place_at_grid(simulation, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)

outline.topic: The Curious Link: Elastic Collisions and the Digits of Pi
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in physics and mathematics

sections.title: Prerequisite: Elastic Collisions
sections.content: Define 1D elastic collisions. Explain conservation of momentum and kinetic energy. Introduce the scenario: a small block (mass m) hitting a large block (mass M) toward a wall.
sections.example: A toy car (m=1kg) hits a heavy crate (M=100kg) that is sliding toward a solid brick wall.

sections.title: The Collisional Setup
sections.content: Visualize the geometry. We track the number of collisions between two blocks (m and M) and a wall. As M becomes significantly larger than m, the number of collisions changes unexpectedly.
sections.example: Imagine a tiny hamster (m) bouncing between a giant sumo wrestler (M) and a wall. We count every 'thud' of the hamster.

sections.title: The Mathematical Mapping
sections.content: Introduce the mind-bending result: when M = 100^n * m, the total number of collisions is the first n+1 digits of Pi (π). Explain that the phase space of the system maps to the geometry of a circle.
sections.example: If the mass ratio is 1:100, there are exactly 31 collisions (3.1... the first digits of π).

sections.title: Visualizing the Unfolding
sections.content: Explain the trajectory in 2D space. The velocity of the blocks can be represented as a vector bouncing within a wedge. The angle of the wedge is defined by the mass ratio, effectively 'measuring' π.
sections.example: An animated 'bouncing light beam' inside a wedge where the beam hits the edges exactly π/θ times.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition
sections.content: Summarize how physical conservation laws act as a 'calculator' for transcendental numbers. Highlight that nature often hides mathematical constants in the most chaotic-looking mechanical systems.
sections.example: Summarizing the 'Sumo-Hamster' simulation: The heavier the wrestler, the more digits of π we reveal through the hamster's path.
